title: Query-complexity-aware SLI and predictive circuit-breaker policy
creator: Lena Chen
description:
Context:
Redwood currently defines SLIs primarily by endpoint and model-variant without accounting for request complexity. This causes two operational problems: (1) high-complexity requests (long contexts, multimodal payloads, code-generation) systematically burn SLOs and error budgets faster than short text requests, and (2) fixed circuit-breaker thresholds either overreact to short bursts of cheap requests or underreact to heavy expensive workloads.

Goal:
Define a per-endpoint, per-model SLI taxonomy that is query-complexity aware, add a predictive circuit-breaker policy that uses short-term load forecasting and complexity-weighted capacity accounting, and codify an error-budget burn/recovery policy tied to complexity buckets and multi-region failover. The aim is to improve fairness across tenants, reduce unnecessary failovers, and provide clearer operational levers for CapacityOps.

Key definitions proposed:
- Complexity Score (CS): single numeric score computed at request admission. CS = w1*token_count_normalized + w2*multimodal_flag + w3*structured_output_flag + w4*avg_generation_temp_factor + w5*specialized_op_flag (e.g., code, embeddings + gen). Initial weights: w1=0.6, w2=0.15, w3=0.1, w4=0.1, w5=0.05. Values normalized to [0,1].
- Complexity Buckets: LOW (CS <= 0.25), MEDIUM (0.25 < CS <= 0.6), HIGH (CS > 0.6).
- Composite SLI: a request is counted as SLI-success if BOTH: (a) latency requirement met for the bucket AND (b) model-quality sentinel passes (see Quality SLI below).
- Latency targets (initial): LOW p95 < 60ms, MEDIUM p95 < 180ms, HIGH p95 < 450ms.
- Quality SLI: measured via live lightweight heuristics (e.g., hallucination-detector score, truncated embedding-similarity to reference prompts when available, and model self-consistency checks) as a pass/fail signal. Initial target: quality-pass-rate >= 99% for LOW, 97% MEDIUM, 95% HIGH.

Circuit-breaker / predictive load-shedding policy:
1) Admission control uses Complexity-Weighted QPS (CWQ): CWQ = sum over active requests of CS * model_cost_factor. Model_cost_factor is per-variant (e.g., 1 for base-7B, 3 for 13B quantized, 8 for 70B float).
2) Per-region soft thresholds: region_capacity_score computed from active GPU slots and recent per-GPU throughput. If CWQ > 0.8 * provisioned_capacity -> enter Degraded Mode (apply gentle shedding: 10-30% tail-drop on LOW priority tokens and deprioritize background batch jobs). If CWQ > 1.05 * provisioned_capacity -> Hard Tripped (invoke circuit breaker).
3) Predictive component: 1-min EWMA forecast of CWQ and a 30s anomaly detector (z-score over rolling 2-min window). If forecast shows >15% increase in next minute AND current utilization >65%, pre-emptively reduce admitted low-priority traffic by X% and notify CapacityOps.
4) Graceful fallback: circuit breaker first attempts model-variant fallback (to cheaper quantized variant) if quality SLI forecast indicates degradation < quality tolerance. If no suitable fallback, route to warm-standby region per regional-failover matrix.

Error budget accounting and burn policy:
- Error budget units are tracked separately per complexity-bucket for each endpoint-model. That is, we maintain 3 parallel error budgets: EB_LOW, EB_MED, EB_HIGH. This prevents cheap requests from consuming budgets needed for heavy requests.
- Burn rate calculation uses complexity-weighted failures: each failed request consumes CS units from bucket budget instead of 1. Time-windowed burn-rate alerts (1h and 24h windows) trigger mitigation steps.
- Cross-region borrowing: if a region exhausts EB_HIGH for a critical endpoint, it can borrow up to 20% of another region's EB_HIGH subject to global reserve. Borrowing requires: (a) customer has multi-region allowance, (b) borrower not in immediate emergency. Borrow transactions are logged and periodically reconciled.

Instrumentation & telemetry changes required:
- Admission path must emit CS and chosen model_cost_factor per request (new fields: admission.cs, admission.variant_cost_factor).
- SLIs must be recorded with complexity_bucket tag and quality_pass boolean. Logs and prom metrics: slo.success{endpoint,model,complexity_bucket}, slo.latency_ms{quantiles,endpoint,model,complexity_bucket}, slo.quality_pass_rate{...}.
- Circuit-breaker decisions emitted as events with reason and pre/post CWQ.

Dashboards & Alerts:
- New dashboard: "Complexity SLI & Capacity" with per-endpoint heatmap of EB consumption by bucket, per-region CWQ, predictive_trend, and circuit status.
- Alerting: EB burn-rate (1h) on any bucket > 3x expected triggers throttled mitigations; EB exhaustion triggers PagerDuty to CapacityOps for P1 endpoints only.

Rollout plan / migration strategy:
1) Beta on internal endpoints: enable CS emission and bucketized SLIs for a small set of endpoints (metrics-only, no enforcement) for 2 weeks.
2) Canary enforcement: apply soft shedding rules in one non-critical region for 72h. Observe impact on latency & quality.
3) Full enforcement: enable across all regions with predictive breakers and regional borrowing.

Open trade-offs / questions:
- We are introducing complexity into SLI definition which increases alerting and interpretation cost. Need to verify if teams prefer bucketed SLIs vs per-request weighting in a single SLI.
- Quality SLI heuristics are approximate; we must guard against false positives causing budget burns. Consider a slow path to compute higher fidelity quality signals for a subset of requests.
- Borrowing policy edge cases (simultaneous exhaustion) — need global reserve sizing. Recommend initial reserve = 5% of global EB per critical product.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/resilience/query-complexity-sli (design draft)
- Prototype PR (admission + metrics): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4132
- Dashboard mock: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd123/complexity-sli
- Load-shedding simulator (notebooks): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1Qw-shed-sim

Acceptance criteria:
- Complexity score emitted for 99% of traffic in beta endpoints with <1% overhead added to admission latency.
- Per-bucket SLI metrics available in Prometheus/Grafana and historical EB burn plots for last 30 days.
- Circuit-breaker predictive rule correctly reduces admissions for synthetic spike in simulator in 3/5 runs with no quality-regression when fallback to cheaper variant is applied.

Next steps (owner: Marco Rios):
- (Week 1) Implement admission.cs emission and add metrics counters (PR #4132 review feedback).
- (Week 2) Wire up Prom rules and create dashboard. Run internal beta for 2 weeks.
- (Week 4) Evaluate results and iterate on weights for CS; prepare canary enforcement.

Long-term: consider integrating a learned Complexity predictor (small model) in admission path to better classify expensive requests (defer to 2H 2026 roadmap).
